Inside `createMigrateDownCommandHandler`, `const identity = migrationCommandIdentity(input, projectId)` moved from ABOVE the databaseUrl/workspace/projectRoot composition check to BELOW it. migrate-down-admission.ts IS UNTOUCHED, deliberately. `migrationCommandIdentity` is a pure admission function with no view of composition; reordering inside it would have broken migrate-down-admission.test.ts and rollback-command's parallel shape. The comment also records that the operator-principal fence still answers first, so an unauthenticated caller never observes UNCONFIGURED. FOLLOW-UP THIS ROW DELIBERATELY DID NOT TAKE (a follow-up item, not a new row — EVIDENCE-IS-NOT-ITS-OWN-ROW rail).

A BROKER PROTOCOL-VERSION HANDSHAKE IN `packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-broker-path.ts`, so a stale `.exe` is refused BY NAME AT RESOLUTION instead of at first launch.

The defect this row repaired had a 13-day-old `dist/windows-job-native/release/moe-windows-job-broker.exe` resolving perfectly and then answering UnknownCommand to `APPROVED_IMAGE_LAUNCH_OPCODE = 4`, surfacing as `PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_REFUSED / BROKER_PROTOCOL` three layers from the cause. `resolveBrokerBinary` checks EXISTENCE, never CURRENCY, so it cannot refuse. Missing-binary and stale-binary are different defects with opposite symptoms: a missing binary refuses loudly and locally at resolution (`…_BROKER_UNRESOLVED`); a stale one resolves fine and refuses quietly and distantly. That difference is what sent three earlier sessions after three wrong causes (missing binary, non-win32 platform, test-expectation defect) and cost this board most of a day.

SHAPE: have the broker answer a version/capability opcode at resolution and refuse with a named code (e.g. `PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_STALE`) carrying the supported and required opcode sets, so the failure names the artifact and the fix (`cargo build`) rather than the wire symptom.

WHY NOT HERE: it is a production change to the SHARED resolution seam with its own boundary and smoke suites, and it is not what DoD 1 needed. DoD 1 asked for the port's own containment reason to be named, and the port ALREADY returns `refusal: {code, layer}` — only the two fixtures discarded it. Naming it there was the smallest production-reachable slice (DELIVERY BIAS rail) and is now done: the failure reads `scoped criterion execution did not prove all checks; execution port refused PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_REFUSED at layer BROKER_PROTOCOL`, drilled red in step 6.

ALSO REJECTED AT PLAN TIME, recorded so it is not re-litigated: adding a `refusal` field to `CriterionResult` so the code reaches the durable evidence record. `git grep -ln outputSha256 -- apps/daemon packages` names 21 asserting files (runs-read, node-verifier, v2-readiness-evidence-producers, review-test-fixtures, repository-recovery-test-fixtures, release-durable-facts, criterion-receipt, …). A returned-shape change across 21 consumers is a plan-time SPLIT signal under the shape rail, not a step in this row.

STANDING HOST HAZARD worth a line in the runbook: `dist/` is gitignored, so landing a commit that changes the Rust source can never refresh the built artifact on a dev host, and `git status` stays clean the whole time. CI rebuilds it (`.github/workflows/cross-host.yml:293`); the local dev loop does not. Detection in one step is `ls -la <artifact>` versus `git log -S "<NewSymbol>" -- <source>` — artifact older than the symbol's commit means stale.
